specNotes: Protocol validity is based on the pinned IAB AdCOM 1.0 primary contract, not on current Core output. Optional-field warnings do not make this pair invalid.

AdCOM Placement.display contains DisplayPlacement.nativefmt, whose NativeFormat.asset array specifies AssetFormat entries. The response uses Ad.display.native, whose Native.asset array supplies the matching Asset entries. Native is a display subtype; neither Placement.native nor Ad.native is a standard field.

Each AssetFormat contains exactly one subtype and the response supplies all three requested IDs: title.text within title.len, image.url with the requested 1x1 dimensions, and data.value within data.len. Request img and response image are the different field names prescribed by their respective AdCOM tables.

AdCOM Display permits exactly one creative representation: banner, native, adm or curl. This structured native response therefore legitimately omits adm and curl; requiring either field is a product validation error.

The expected native-completeness verdict is justified by the three required request assets and matching response assets. The current 3.0 crosscheck projector omits native assets, which is tracked as a missing capability independently of the valid payload.
Floor and currency are USD throughout so this pair does not also exercise the separate flrcur currency-plugin gap DEF-105.
The original embedded 1x1 PNG data URI matches the 1x1 dimensions declared on both sides and permits image-load verification without network access.

The centralized browser audit must remeasure the corrected AdCOM envelopes. The existing browser gap records empty preview/source-selection behavior; its guard must still reproduce after this fixture correction.
Inspect the intended click target without following it.
